conventions.convention: Knots are smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. Connected sum uses a fixed orientation-reversing boundary identification, symmetric under interchange and compatible with the fixed mirror reflection. Prime knots are required to be nontrivial.
A PL embedding has a subpolyhedral image and a PL inverse onto that image; the ambient triangulations and subdivisions are finite on the compact spaces considered.

A parametrized PL ball includes an actual finite PL homeomorphism with PL inverse to a convex ball. Window removal uses the closure of the set difference and requires the displayed local quadrant condition.
The PL Loop theorem starts with a supplied finite compatible orientable manifold triangulation. Boundary classes are tested outside a normal subgroup, independently of basepath conjugation.
The ribbon disk uses the standard radial function on the four-ball, with interior Morse critical points of indices zero and one and no interior maxima.
The positive-push Seifert pairing is V_ij = lk(a_i^+,a_j), Alexander polynomials are considered up to units ±t^k, and signature at −1 is the signature of 2(V+V^T).
The knot structural results assume countable choice. Exact trefoil genus, trefoil primality, the examples, and TOP three-manifold prime decomposition explicitly assume full AC.
TOP connected-sum spheres and balls are tame, meaning locally flat; boundary is allowed and original spherical boundary components are retained.

load_bearing.statement: Assume countable choice. Let S ⊂ S³ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard S². There is a smooth ambient isotopy starting at the identity taking S to the standard equatorial sphere; both complementary closures are standard smooth balls, with compatible boundary and collar identifications.

Prescribed PL maps between boundary disks of parametrized PL three-balls extend over the balls; gluing along such disks gives a parametrized PL ball; removal leaves a parametrized PL ball under the stated standard boundary-window condition.

A surjective PL height on a compact finite polyhedron has a finite height-preserving global product parameter when every fiber has the stated local PL collars in both adjacent sublevel and superlevel sets, with one-sided conditions at endpoints.

If n(S,h)>0, two supplied finite PL embedded spheres admit generic affine heights with n(S′₁,h₁)+n(S′₂,h₂)≤n(S,h)−1, and supplied parametrized balls for those spheres reconstruct a parametrized ball for S.

A supplied finite PL embedding of the standard PL two-sphere in R³ bounds a compact parametrized PL three-ball; in standard PL S³ it bounds two parametrized PL three-balls and is carried to the standard double boundary by a finite PL homeomorphism. No choice hypothesis is introduced.

For the stated compact connected orientable finitely triangulated PL three-manifold, marked boundary subsurface F and normal subgroup N, a continuous disk map with boundary in Int F outside N yields a properly embedded PL disk with boundary in Int F outside N.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For any smooth oriented knots K,J ⊂ S³, g(K#J)=g(K)+g(J).

For two finite prime decomposing sphere systems of a smooth oriented knot under countable choice, the stated innermost-disk and maximal-factor-ball replacements preserve the unordered list of capped prime oriented knot classes.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Every nontrivial smooth oriented knot in S³ is ambient isotopic to a finite connected sum of prime knots, uniquely up to permutation and orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of the oriented factors.
Assume countable choice. For the standard right-handed trefoil T, its mirror T* and reversed mirror −T*, T#(−T*) bounds a smooth ribbon disk in B⁴.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 says that a reversed round-circle orientation is corrected by “a half-turn in its plane”. Rotation within the circle's plane preserves its orientation. The required ambient orientation-preserving half-turn is about a diameter, as correctly described in lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot, Proof 2.1.

F2 restates lem-two-finite-linear-subdivisions-have-a-common-simplicial-refinement as applying to “two finite linear triangulations of the same polyhedron”, and Proof 2.1 applies it directly to T and T₀. The supplier Statement explicitly starts with two subdivisions of a fixed finite Euclidean simplicial complex. The consumer has not shown that T and T₀ satisfy that extra premise. A short finite intersection-cell triangulation argument supplies the desired refinement, but the cited statement alone is narrower than F2.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite page fixes smooth oriented knots, chosen tubular exteriors and peripheral orientations. The batch's knot prime-decomposition proof does not infer exterior irreducibility or boundary incompressibility from those definitions.

Genus is the minimum over connected compact oriented embedded spanning surfaces under countable choice. The Seifert algorithm supplies an upper bound; exact trefoil genus is separately proved using the explicitly full-AC nonsliceness input.

The multiplication corollary uses the fixed oriented connected-sum construction and local-choice independence, with full AC supplying countable choice. Conversely, the batch's granny/square counterexample uses its actual block-sum and determinant interfaces with the same unit conventions.
The unit-slope lemma uses the standard oriented unknot convention. The genus formula uses mirror/reversal invariance only to transfer genus across parameter-sign changes.

Actual citations use smooth Schoenflies for smooth balls, relative surface transversality for smooth general position, and the PL Loop theorem only after a supplied finite triangulation. Transport of a PL disk is explicitly described as TOP rather than silently smooth. Subcomplex refinement is used for finite PL carriers.

The reverse-mirror and concordance constructions preserve the fixed reflection and oriented gluing convention. The abelian-group theorem uses associativity, commutativity and unknot identity under countable choice; its general ribbon construction is separately supplied.
Exterior irreducibility cites both smooth ball sides from Schoenflies. Boundary incompressibility uses the genus-zero/unknot criterion with its countable-choice hypothesis discharged by full AC.

The normal-surface items use finite PL subcomplex refinement, marked ball-window gluing and supplied sphere parameters. The smooth meridian-disk criterion uses the smooth genus-zero/unknot equivalence, preserving the category distinction.

Descending and bridge-one arguments use the smooth disk criterion. Bridge normalization and bridge additivity retain the two punctures, oriented capped factors, simultaneous smooth ball parameters and countable-choice assumptions of their cited suppliers.
